cues.en: The grand-daddy of neural networks in recommender systems is the Restricted Boltzmann Machine, or RBM for short.
cues.zh: 推薦系統神經網路的老祖宗，是受限玻爾茲曼機，簡稱 RBM。

cues.en: It's been in use since 2007, long before AI had its big resurgence but it's still a commonly cited paper and a technique that's still in use today.
cues.zh: 從 2007 年就開始使用，遠早於 AI 再度大熱門，但仍經常被引用，至今也仍使用。

cues.en: Going back to the Netflix Prize, the main things Netflix learned was that matrix factorization and RBM's had the best performance as measured by RMSE, and their scores were almost identical.
cues.zh: 回到 Netflix Prize，Netflix 主要學到的是：以 RMSE 衡量，矩陣分解與 RBM 表現最好，分數幾乎相同。

cues.en: Again, this shouldn't surprise us too much since we know that you can model matrix factorization as a neural network.
cues.zh: 同樣，不必太驚訝，因為矩陣分解也能建模成神經網路。

cues.en: But they found that by combining matrix factorization with RBM's, the two of them working together provided even better results, they went from an RMSE of 8.9 to 8.8.
cues.zh: 但它們發現，把矩陣分解與 RBM 結合，兩者合作，結果更好，RMSE 從 8.9 降到 8.8。

cues.en: A few years ago, Netflix confirmed they were still using RBM's as part of their recommender system that's in production.
cues.zh: 幾年前，Netflix 確認，正式環境推薦系統，仍使用 RBM 作為其中一部分。

cues.en: Let's learn how it works.
cues.zh: 來學如何運作。

cues.en: First of all, if you're serious about using RBM's for recommendations, I recommend tracking down this paper so you can study it later once you understand the general concepts.
cues.zh: 首先，如果認真想用 RBM 推薦，建議找到這篇論文，了解一般概念後，再深入研究。

cues.en: It's from a team from the University of Toronto, and was published in the Proceedings of the 24th International Conference on Machine Learning in 2007.
cues.zh: 來自多倫多大學團隊，2007 年發表於第二十四屆國際機器學習研討會論文集。

cues.en: If you just Google for the title of the paper Restricted Boltzmann Machines for Collaborative Filtering, you should find a free PDF copy of it, that's from the author's page on the University of Toronto website,
cues.zh: 只要搜尋標題 Restricted Boltzmann Machines for Collaborative Filtering，應該就能找到免費 PDF，來自多倫多大學作者網頁，

cues.en: so I think it's legitimately free for you there.
cues.zh: 所以我認為那裡是合法免費提供。

cues.en: RBM's are really one of the simplest neural networks, it's just two layers, a visible layer and a hidden layer.
cues.zh: RBM 其實是最簡單的神經網路之一，只有兩層，可見層與隱藏層。

cues.en: We train it by feeding our training data into the visible layer in a forward pass, and training weights and biases between them during backpropagation.
cues.zh: 訓練時，前向傳播把訓練資料送進可見層，再於反向傳播，訓練層間權重與偏差。

cues.en: An activation function such as ReLU is used to produce the output from each hidden neuron.
cues.zh: 用 ReLU 等激活函數，產生各隱藏神經元輸出。

cues.en: Why are they called Restricted Boltzmann Machines?
cues.zh: 為什麼叫受限玻爾茲曼機？

cues.en: Well, they are restricted because neurons in the same layer can't communicate with each other directly.
cues.zh: 「受限」，因為同一層神經元，不能直接互相通訊。

cues.en: There are only connections between the two different layers.
cues.zh: 只有兩個不同層之間有連線。

cues.en: That's just what you do these days with modern neural networks, but that restriction didn't exist with earlier Boltzmann Machines back when AI was still kind of floundering as a field.
cues.zh: 現代神經網路通常就是這樣，但早期玻爾茲曼機，在 AI 還發展不順時，沒有這種限制。

cues.en: And RBM's weren't invented by a guy named Boltzmann, the name refers to the Boltzmann distribution function they used for their sampling function.
cues.zh: RBM 也不是叫 Boltzmann 的人發明，而是取自取樣所用的玻爾茲曼分布函數。

cues.en: RBM's are actually credited to Geoffrey Hinston who was a professor at Carnegie Mellon University at the time, the idea actually dates back to 1985.
cues.zh: RBM 通常歸功於當時任教卡內基美隆大學的 Geoffrey Hinton，概念其實可追溯到 1985 年。

cues.en: So, RBM's get trained by doing a forward pass, which we just described, and then a backward pass, where the inputs get reconstructed.
cues.zh: 訓練 RBM，先做剛才描述的前向傳播，再反向傳播，重建輸入。

cues.en: We do this iteratively over many epochs, just like when we train a deep neural network, until it converges on a set of weights and biases that minimizes the error.
cues.zh: 像訓練深度神經網路一樣，多個週期反覆執行，直到收斂到讓誤差最小的一組權重與偏差。

cues.en: Let's take a closer look at that backward pass.
cues.zh: 仔細看看反向傳播。

cues.en: During the backward pass, we are trying to reconstruct the original input by feeding back the output of the forward pass back through the hidden layer, and seeing what values we end up with out of the visible layer.
cues.zh: 我們把前向輸出送回隱藏層，試圖重建原始輸入，看看最後從可見層得到什麼值。

cues.en: Since those weights are initially random, there can be a big difference between the inputs we started with and the ones we reconstruct.
cues.zh: 因為權重一開始隨機，原始輸入與重建輸入，可能差很多。

cues.en: In the process, we end up with another set of bias terms, this time on the visible layer.
cues.zh: 過程中，又得到另一組偏差項，這次在可見層。

cues.en: So, we share weights between both the forward and backward passes, but we have two sets of biases.
cues.zh: 因此，前向與反向共用權重，但有兩組偏差。

cues.en: The hidden bias that's used in the forward pass, and the visible bias used in this backward pass.
cues.zh: 前向使用隱藏偏差，反向使用可見偏差。

cues.en: We can then measure the error we end up with and use that information to adjust the weights a little bit during the next iteration to try and minimize that error.
cues.zh: 接著衡量誤差，用這些資訊，在下一次迭代稍微調整權重，試著讓誤差最小。

cues.en: Conceptually, you can see it's not too different from what we call a linear threshold unit in more modern terminology.
cues.zh: 概念上，與現代術語所說的線性門檻單元，沒有太大不同。

cues.en: You can also construct multi-layer RBM's that are akin to modern deep learning architectures.
cues.zh: 也能建立多層 RBM，類似現代深度學習架構。

cues.en: The main difference is that we read the output of an RBM on the lower level during a backward pass, as opposed to just taking outputs on the other side like we would with a modern neural network.
cues.zh: 主要差異，是 RBM 在反向傳播時，從下層讀取輸出，而不是像現代神經網路，直接從另一端取輸出。

cues.en: So this all works well when you have a complete set of training data, for example, applying an RBM to the same MNIST handwriting recognition problem we looked at in our deep learning intro section
cues.zh: 完整訓練資料時，一切運作良好，例如對深度學習入門看過的 MNIST 手寫辨識問題，使用 RBM，

cues.en: is a straightforward thing to do.
cues.zh: 很直接。

cues.en: When you apply RBM's, or neural networks in general, to recommender systems though, things get weird.
cues.zh: 但把 RBM，或一般神經網路，用到推薦系統，事情就奇怪了。

cues.en: The problem is that we now have sparse training data very sparse, in most cases.
cues.zh: 問題是，訓練資料現在很稀疏，多數情況非常稀疏。

cues.en: How do you train a neural network when most of your inputs nodes have no data to work with?
cues.zh: 大部分輸入節點沒資料時，如何訓練神經網路？

cues.en: Adapting an RBM for, say, recommending movies given five-star ratings data, requires a few twists to the generic RBM architecture we just described.
cues.zh: 要把 RBM 調整成例如根據五星評分推薦電影，需要對一般架構做些變化。

cues.en: Let's take a step back and think about what we're doing here.
cues.zh: 退一步，想想做什麼。

cues.en: The general idea is to use each individual user in our training data as a set of inputs into our RBM to help train it.
cues.zh: 一般概念，是把訓練資料中的每位使用者，當成 RBM 的一組輸入，協助訓練。

cues.en: So, we process each user as part of a batch during training, looking at their ratings for every movie they rated.
cues.zh: 因此，訓練時，將使用者作為批次的一部分，查看他對每部已評分電影的評分。

cues.en: So, our visible nodes represent ratings for a given user on every movie, and we're trying to learn weights and biases to let us reconstruct ratings for user/movie pairs we don't know yet.
cues.zh: 可見節點，代表某位使用者對每部電影的評分，要學習權重與偏差，重建未知的使用者／電影配對評分。

cues.en: First of all, our visible units aren't just simple nodes taking in a single input.
cues.zh: 首先，可見單元，不只是接受單一輸入的簡單節點。

cues.en: Ratings are really categorical data, so we actually want to treat each individual rating as five nodes, one for each possible rating value.
cues.zh: 評分其實是類別資料，因此把每筆評分視為五個節點，每個代表一種可能評分。

cues.en: So, let's say the first rating we have in our training data is a five-star rating, that would be represented as four nodes with a value of zero and one with a value of one, as represented here.
cues.zh: 假設訓練資料第一筆是五星，就像這樣，表示成四個零節點，加一個一節點。

cues.en: Then we have a couple of ratings that are missing for user/item pairs that are unknown and need to be predicted.
cues.zh: 接著，有兩筆未知使用者／項目配對的缺失評分，需要預測。

cues.en: Then we have a three-star rating, represented like this with a one in the third slot.
cues.zh: 再來，是三星評分，第三個位置是一，像這樣。

cues.en: When we're done training the RBM, we'll have a set of weights and biases that should allow us to reconstruct ratings for any user.
cues.zh: 訓練完成後，就有一組能重建任何使用者評分的權重與偏差。

cues.en: So to use it to predict ratings for a new user, we just run it once again using the known ratings of the user we're interested in.
cues.zh: 要預測新使用者，只要用目標使用者的已知評分，再執行一次。

cues.en: We run those through in the forward pass, then back again in the backward pass, to end up with reconstructed rating values for that user.
cues.zh: 先前向，再反向，最後得到該使用者的重建評分。

cues.en: We can then run softmax on each group of five rating values to translate the output back into a five-star rating for every item.
cues.zh: 再對每組五個評分值，使用 softmax，把輸出轉回每個項目的五星評分。

cues.en: But again, the big problem is that the data we have is sparse.
cues.zh: 但再次強調，最大問題是資料稀疏。

cues.en: If we are training an RBM on every possible combination of users and movies, most of that data will be missing, because most movies have not been rated at all by a specific user.
cues.zh: 若對所有使用者與電影組合訓練，大部分資料都缺失，因為某位使用者，大部分電影都沒評分。

cues.en: We want to predict user ratings for every movie though, so we need to leave space for all of them.
cues.zh: 但想預測每部電影，所以需要為所有電影留空間。

cues.en: That means if we have N movies, we end up with N time five visible nodes, and for any given user, most of them are undefined and empty.
cues.zh: 有 N 部電影，就有 N 乘五個可見節點，對任何使用者，大部分未定義、為空。

cues.en: We deal with this by excluding any missing ratings from processing while we're training the RBM.
cues.zh: 訓練時，排除所有缺失評分的處理，來解決。

cues.en: This is kind of a tricky thing to do, because most frameworks built for DeepLearning such as TensorFlow assume you want to process everything in parallel, all the time.
cues.zh: 有點棘手，因為 TensorFlow 等深度學習框架，假設你想隨時平行處理所有資料。

cues.en: Sparse data isn't something they were really built for originally, but there are ways to trick it into doing what we want.
cues.zh: 原本不是為稀疏資料打造，但有辦法讓它做想要的事。

cues.en: But, notice that we've only drawn lines between visible units that actually have known ratings data in them, and the hidden layer.
cues.zh: 注意，圖中只在有已知評分的可見單元，與隱藏層之間畫連線。

cues.en: So as we're training our RBM with a given user's known ratings, we only attempt to learn the weights and biases used for the movies that user actually rated.
cues.zh: 因此，以某位使用者的已知評分訓練時，只學習他實際評分電影相關的權重與偏差。

cues.en: As we iterate through training on all of the other users, we fill in the other weights and biases as we go.
cues.zh: 隨著迭代訓練其他使用者，逐漸填入其他權重與偏差。

cues.en: For the sake of completeness, I should point out that TensorFlow actually does have a sparse tensor these days you can use, and there are other frameworks such as Amazon's DSSTNE
cues.zh: 為求完整，要指出，現在 TensorFlow 其實有 SparseTensor，也有 Amazon DSSTNE 等框架，

cues.en: system that are designed to construct more typical deep neural networks with sparse data.
cues.zh: 專門以稀疏資料，建立較典型深度神經網路。

cues.en: RBM's will probably become a thing of the past now that we can treat sparse data in the same manner as complete data with modern neural networks, and we will examine that in more depth
cues.zh: 既然現代神經網路，能像完整資料一樣處理稀疏資料，RBM 可能會成為過去；之後課程，

cues.en: in an upcoming section of this course.
cues.zh: 會深入研究。

cues.en: The other twist is how to best train an RBM that contains huge amounts of sparse data.
cues.zh: 另一個變化，是如何最好地訓練包含大量稀疏資料的 RBM。

cues.en: Gradient descent needs a very efficient expectation function to optimize on, and for recommender systems this function is called contrastive divergence.
cues.zh: 梯度下降，需要非常有效率的期望函數來最佳化；對推薦系統，這個函數叫做對比散度。

cues.en: At least, that's the function the paper on the topic uses successfully.
cues.zh: 至少，那篇論文成功使用了它。

cues.en: The math behind it gets a bit complicated, but the basic idea is that it samples probability distributions during training using something called a Gibbs sampler.
cues.zh: 背後數學有點複雜，但基本上，訓練時，用 Gibbs 取樣器，對機率分布取樣。

cues.en: We only train it on the ratings that actually exist, but re-use the resulting weights and biases across other users to fill in the missing ratings we want to predict.
cues.zh: 只用實際存在的評分訓練，但跨使用者重用權重與偏差，填入想預測的缺失評分。

cues.en: So, let's look at some code that actually implements an RBM on our MovieLens data, and play around with it!
cues.zh: 看看真正對 MovieLens 實作 RBM 的程式碼，實驗一下。
